digest:
- US commercial auto insurance rates increased 6.7% in Q3 2026 despite an overall 1.3% decline in commercial P&C premiums, supporting strong rate adequacy for Nirvana's last-mile products [9].
- The Trump administration finalized a rule making it easier to classify workers as independent contractors, stabilizing the contracted fleet business model and commercial auto policy demand for owner-operators [6, 7].
- Amazon warned customers and threatened to leave NYC over a proposed Delivery Protection Act mandating direct employment, which threatens the local DSP contractor model and urban fleet density Nirvana plans to underwrite [1, 4, 5].

new.title: Amazon threatens NYC orders could be $5 more if Council bill passes
new.summary: Amazon warned NYC customers of potential five-dollar fee hikes if a bill passes requiring retailers to directly employ delivery workers rather than use contractors.
new.evidence_quote: law requiring retailers to directly employ delivery workers rather than contract out the work
new.implication: Mandating direct employment would dismantle the DSP contractor model in NYC, consolidating auto liability onto Amazon and threatening independent fleet insurance demand.

new.title: Amazon app warns New York of higher costs if Mamdani delivery law passes
new.summary: Amazon is actively lobbying against New York City delivery legislation that is supported by the mayor, warning users about higher delivery expenses.

new.implication: Persistent municipal efforts to eliminate contracted delivery models in NYC threaten the viability of local Amazon DSP fleets Nirvana plans to underwrite.

new.title: Proposed NYC delivery worker safety bill sparks debate over jobs and small businesses

new.evidence_quote: Proposed NYC delivery worker safety bill sparks debate over jobs and small businesses
new.implication: Direct employment mandates could restructure DSP operating models, affecting fleet commercial auto insurance structures.

new.title: Amazon threatens to leave NYC again, this time over delivery bill, as it rallies customers to fight it
